questions.solution:
For reaction:& ${SO}_{2 ( g )} + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2 ( g )} ⇌ {SO}_{3 ( g )}$

The relation between equilibrium constant in terms of pressures~${K}_{p}$~and equilibrium constant in terms of concentration~${K}_{c}$~is

${K}_{p} = {K}_{c} \times ( RT{)}^{∆ ng}$

$⇒ 2 \times {10}^{12} = {K}_{c} \times ( 0 . 082 \times 300{)}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ {K}_{C} = 0 . 992 \times {10}^{13}$

So, answer is 1.

At $298K$, the equilibrium constant is $2 \times {10}^{15}$ for the reaction:

$Cu \left(s\right) + 2{Ag}^{+} \left($aq\right) ⇌ {Cu}^{2 $+}\left($aq\right) + $2Ag\left($s\right)$

The equilibrium constant for the reaction

\dfrac{1}{2}{Cu}^{2 +} \left($aq\right) + Ag \left(s\right) ⇌ \dfrac{1}{2}Cu\left(s\right) + {Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right)$~is $x \times {10}^{- 8}$. The value of $x$ \text{ and } is ______. (Round off the answer to the nearest integer)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$

$Cu\left(s\right) + 2{Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right) ⇌ {Cu}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + 2Ag\left(s\right); {K}_{eq} = 2 \times {10}^{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}{Cu}^{2 +} \left(aq\right) + Ag \left($s\right) ⇌ $\ddfrac{1}{2}Cu\left(s\right) + {Ag}^{+}\left(aq\right)$

The equilibrium reaction is reversed and multiplied with~$\dfrac{1}{2},$

Hence,~${K}_{eq}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{{K}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times {10}^{15}} =x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{20} \times \dfrac{1}{107} =x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{20} \times {10}^{- 7} =x \times {10}^{- 8}$

$\dfrac{10}{20} =x$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{10}{2} = \sqrt{5} =2 . 236$

$≃ 2 . 24$

$

questions.q: The following concentrations were observed at $500K$ for the formation of ${NH}_{3}$ from ${N}_{2}$ and ${H}_{2}$. At equilibrium : \left[{N}_{2}\right] = 2 \times {10}^{- 2}M, \left[{H}_{2}\right] = 3 \times {10}^{- 2}M$ and \left[{NH}_{3}\right] = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}M$. Equilibrium constant for the reaction is ______.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The equilibrium constant of concentration (denoted by ${K}_{c}$) of a chemical reaction at equilibrium can be defined as the ratio of the concentration of products to the concentration of the reactants, each raised to their respective stoichiometric coefficients.

The equilibrium reaction is

${N}_{2\left(g\right)} + 3{H}_{2\left(g\right)}\mathop{⇋}_{}^{}2{NH}_{3\left(g\right)}$

${K}_{c} = \dfrac{\left[{NH}_{3}\right]2}{\left[{H}_{2}\right]3\left[{N}_{2}\right]}$

$= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2}{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)3 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$= \dfrac{{3}^{2} \times {10}^{- 4}}{{2}^{2} \times {3}^{3} \times {10}^{- 6} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4 \times 2 \times 3} \times {10}^{4} = \dfrac{10000}{24} = 416 . 6 \approx 417$

Assume only methanol is formed as the product and the system follows ideal gas behaviour.

($\begin{array}{llll}
& \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) & + & 2 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) & \rightleftharpoons & \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}(\mathrm{g}) \\
\mathrm{t}=0 & 0.1 \mathrm{~mol} & & \mathrm{a} \mathrm{~mol} & & - \\
\mathrm{t}_{\text {eq }} & 0.1-\mathrm{x} & & \mathrm{a}-2 \mathrm{x} & & \mathrm{x}=0.04 \\
& =0.06 & & =\mathrm{a}-0.08 & \\
& & & =0.23-0.08 \\
& & & =0.15 \mathrm{~mole}
\end{array}$)
($\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{V}=2 \mathrm{~L} \\ & \mathrm{~T}=500 \mathrm{~K} \\ & \mathrm{P}_{\text {total }}=5 \mathrm{bar} \\ & \mathrm{n}_{\text {Total }}=0.25=\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{~mol} \\ & \mathrm{P}_{\text {total }}=\mathrm{n}_{\text {total }} \times \frac{\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{V}} \\ & \Rightarrow 5=(0.06+\mathrm{a}-0.08+0.04) \times \frac{0.08 \times 500}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 10=(0.02+\mathrm{a}) \times 0.08 \times 500\end{aligned}$)
(\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=0.25-0.02=0.23 \mathrm{~mol}.)
($\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}}}{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{CO}} \times \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{H}_2}^2} \times \frac{1}{\left(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)^2}=\frac{0.04}{0.06 \times(0.15)^2} \times\left[\frac{1 / 4}{5}\right]^2 \\
& =\frac{4}{6 \times(0.15)^2 \times 16} \times \frac{1}{25} \\
& =\frac{100 \times 100}{24 \times 225 \times 25}=\frac{100 \times 100}{135000} \\
& =0.074=74 \times 10^{-3}
\end{aligned}$)

questions.q:
The stepwise formation of \left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$ is given below:

${Cu}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{K1}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K2}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)2\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)2\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K3}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)3\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)3\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K4}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$

The value of stability constants ${K}_{1}, {K}_{2}, {K}_{3}$ and ${K}_{4}$ are ${10}^{4}, 1 . 58 \times {10}^{3}, 5 \times {10}^{2}$ and ${10}^{2}$~respectively. The overall equilibrium constants for dissociation of \left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$ is $x \times {10}^{- 12} .$~The value of $x$ is \text{ and } _____ \text{ and } (Rounded off to the nearest integer)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${Cu}^{2 +} + {NH}_{3}\overset{K1}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K2}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)2\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)2\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K3}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)3\right]2 +$

\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)3\right]2 + + {NH}_{3}\overset{K4}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$

${Cu}^{2 +} + 4{NH}_{3}\overset{K}{⇌}\left[Cu\left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$

So,

$K = {K}_{1} \times {K}_{2} \times {K}_{3} \times {K}_{4}$

$= {10}^{4} \times 1 .58 \times {10}^{3} \times 5 \times {10}^{2} \times {10}^{2}$

$K = 7 .9 \times {10}^{11}$

Where $K \to$ Equilibrium constant for formation of \left[Cu \left({NH}_{3}\right)4\right]2 +$
So equilibrium constant \left(K^{'}\right)$ for dissociation
$\text{of} \l$left[Cu \left({NH}_{3}\right)$4]2 $+\text{is}\dfrac{1}{K}

$K^{'} = $\dfrac{1}{K}

$K^{'} = $\dfrac{1}{7 . 9 \times {10}^{11}}

$= 1 . 26 $\times {10}^{- 12} = \left($x $\times {10}^{- 12}\right)

So the value of $x = 1 . 26$

$OMR$~Ans $= 1$ \text{ and } (After rounded off to the nearest integer)

$
